259	            _write_package(target, classes, exported, manifest, None)
260	    else:
261	        _write_package(target, classes, exported, manifest, None)

271	                    sorted(distributions[set_name]["distribution"].items())
272	                ),

388	# A resolver maps a full SHA-256 digest to the absolute path of the
389	# sorted-first regular file carrying that content, plus the file's
390	# identity (device, inode) of the proved object actually hashed during
391	# the lookup.  The copy opens that exact inode pinned through the open,
392	# so a swap after the lookup — another regular file, even with
393	# identical content, or a symlink, even one pointing at the original
394	# file — cannot be read in its place; swaps landing in the gap inside
395	# the lookup itself are rejected by the scan before the digest is
396	# recorded.
397	Resolver = dict[str, tuple[Path, int, int]]
398	
399	
400	class _ScanResult(dict):
401	    """The digest resolver, also carrying every real directory seen.
402	
403	    Behaves as the plain digest-to-file resolver mapping, with an extra
404	    ``directory_ids`` attribute: each key is a ``/``-separated path
405	    relative to the root (``""`` for the root itself) and each value is
406	    ``(display path, device, inode)`` as observed during the walk.
407	    """
408	
409	    def __init__(
410	        self,
411	        files: dict[str, tuple[Path, int, int]],
412	        directories: dict[str, tuple[Path, int, int]],
413	    ) -> None:
414	        super().__init__(files)
415	        self.directory_ids = directories
416	
417	
418	def _scan_source_directory(root: Path) -> Resolver:
419	    """Walk ``root`` and map every digest to the sorted-first copy.
420	
421	    The directory and all its subdirectories are searched for regular
422	    files only: there is no extension filter, symlinks and other
423	    non-regular entries are skipped, and the walk never descends through
424	    symlinked directories.  Every regular file found is read in full and
425	    identified by its content digest; when several files share content,
426	    the one whose slash-separated path relative to ``root`` sorts first
427	    by Unicode code point owns the digest.  A directory that cannot be
428	    scanned, an entry that cannot be inspected or a file that cannot be
429	    read in full fails the export with the path and reason.
430	
431	    Each file read is itself pinned through the shared
432	    inspect / open-no-follow-with-nonblocking / fstat-prove rule: the
433	    bytes hashed come from the exact regular file the walk typed, and
434	    an object swapped onto the name in that gap — a named pipe (even
435	    with no writer), a symlink or another regular file, even a
436	    byte-identical one — fails the export before any of its bytes are
437	    read, naming the path and what it became.
438	
439	    Every step is anchored to directory descriptors rather than path
440	    strings: a child is typed and entered with ``fstatat``/``openat``
441	    relative to the descriptor of the directory it was listed from, and
442	    each entered directory is pinned for the whole time its contents are
443	    processed.  A real subdirectory whose path is swapped for a symlink
444	    after it was listed but before or while it is entered therefore can
445	    never be followed — the open refuses the link and the export fails
446	    naming that directory — and a swap landing while its children are
447	    being read is detected when its path binding is re-checked after the
448	    children have been processed.  Only entries that are already
449	    symlinks when first listed are skipped, preserving the original
450	    convention.
451	    """
452	    try:
453	        root_fd = os.open(root, os.O_RDONLY | _O_DIRECTORY)
454	    except OSError as error:
455	        raise ExportError(f"cannot scan directory {root}: {error}") from error
456	    try:
457	        return _scan_tree(root_fd, root)
458	    finally:
459	        os.close(root_fd)
460	
461	
462	def _scan_tree(root_fd: int, root: Path) -> _ScanResult:
463	    """Walk the tree reached through the already-open, pinned ``root_fd``."""
464	    found: dict[str, tuple[str, Path, int, int]] = {}
465	    directories: dict[str, tuple[Path, int, int]] = {}
466	    try:
467	        root_status = os.fstat(root_fd)
468	    except OSError as error:
469	        raise ExportError(f"cannot scan directory {root}: {error}") from error
470	    directories[""] = (root, root_status.st_dev, root_status.st_ino)
471	    _walk_tree(root_fd, root, found, directories)
472	    files = {
473	        digest: (path, device, inode)
474	        for digest, (_, path, device, inode) in found.items()
475	    }
476	    return _ScanResult(files, directories)

479	def _list_directory(directory_fd: int, display: Path) -> list[str]:
480	    """List one pinned directory's entry names, or fail naming the path."""
481	    try:
482	        return [entry.name for entry in os.scandir(directory_fd)]
483	    except OSError as error:
484	        raise ExportError(f"cannot scan directory {display}: {error}") from error

486	
487	def _walk_tree(
488	    root_fd: int,
489	    root: Path,
490	    found: dict[str, tuple[str, Path, int, int]],
491	    directories: dict[str, tuple[Path, int, int]],
492	) -> None:
493	    """Walk the whole tree below the pinned root without Python recursion.
494	
495	    The descent runs on an explicit stack rather than Python calls: a
496	    tree deeper than the interpreter's recursion limit is scanned in
497	    full instead of aborting partway with a ``RecursionError``.  A frame
498	    is one entered directory — the descriptor of the parent it was
499	    listed from, its own pinned descriptor, its parent-relative basename
500	    (``None`` for the root, whose descriptor is owned by the caller),
501	    its display path and the entry names still to visit (reversed, so
502	    ``pop()`` yields scan order).  A parent frame, descriptor still
503	    open, stays on the stack for the whole time its subtree is
504	    processed, so every directory remains pinned exactly as long as with
505	    a recursive walk, at any depth.
506	    """
507	    frames: list[list[Any]] = [
508	        [root_fd, root_fd, None, root, _list_directory(root_fd, root)[::-1]]
509	    ]
510	    try:
511	        while frames:
512	            parent_fd, directory_fd, name, display, entries = frames[-1]
513	            if not entries:
514	                frames.pop()
515	                if name is not None:
516	                    # The children are done and were all reached through
517	                    # this pinned descriptor.  Re-prove the
518	                    # parent-relative name still binds to this same
519	                    # directory: a symlink (or anything else) swapped
520	                    # onto it while the children were being processed
521	                    # must fail the export even though nothing was read
522	                    # through that link.
523	                    try:
524	                        _assert_still_same_directory(
525	                            parent_fd, name, display, directory_fd
526	                        )
527	                    finally:
528	                        os.close(directory_fd)
529	                continue
530	            child_name = entries.pop()
531	            child_display = display / child_name
532	            try:
533	                status = os.stat(
534	                    child_name, dir_fd=directory_fd, follow_symlinks=False
535	                )
536	            except OSError as error:
537	                raise ExportError(
538	                    f"cannot inspect entry {child_display}: {error}"
539	                ) from error
540	            mode = status.st_mode
541	            if stat.S_ISLNK(mode):
542	                # A symlink when first encountered: skipped, never read.
543	                continue
544	            if stat.S_ISREG(mode):
545	                digest, device, inode = _hash_regular_file_at(
546	                    directory_fd, child_name, child_display
547	                )
548	                rel = os.path.relpath(child_display, root).replace(os.sep, "/")
549	                current = found.get(digest)
550	                if current is None or rel < current[0]:
551	                    found[digest] = (rel, child_display, device, inode)
552	            elif stat.S_ISDIR(mode):
553	                child_fd = _enter_subdirectory(
554	                    directory_fd, child_name, child_display
555	                )
556	                transferred = False
557	                try:
558	                    try:
559	                        pinned = os.fstat(child_fd)
560	                    except OSError as error:
561	                        raise ExportError(
562	                            f"cannot scan directory {child_display}: {error}"
563	                        ) from error
564	                    rel = os.path.relpath(child_display, root).replace(
565	                        os.sep, "/"
566	                    )
567	                    directories[rel] = (
568	                        child_display,
569	                        pinned.st_dev,
570	                        pinned.st_ino,
571	                    )
572	                    frames.append(
573	                        [
574	                            directory_fd,
575	                            child_fd,
576	                            child_name,
577	                            child_display,
578	                            _list_directory(child_fd, child_display)[::-1],
579	                        ]
580	                    )
581	                    # The descriptor now belongs to the frame and is
582	                    # closed when that frame finishes; the finally must
583	                    # not close it on the successful path.
584	                    transferred = True
585	                finally:
586	                    if not transferred:
587	                        os.close(child_fd)
588	            # Any other entry type is skipped as before.
589	    finally:
590	        # On a failure mid-walk, close every confirmed descendant
591	        # descriptor still held by an unfinished frame; the root
592	        # descriptor itself is owned by the caller.
593	        for frame in frames:
594	            if frame[2] is not None:
595	                os.close(frame[1])

598	def _enter_subdirectory(parent_fd: int, name: str, display: Path) -> int:
599	    """Open a listed subdirectory relative to ``parent_fd`` and pin it.
600	
601	    The parent listed ``name`` as a real directory, so anything other
602	    than that same directory observed here means the path changed after
603	    the listing.  This is the first confirmation of the directory: no
604	    identity was recorded yet, so the fresh inspection itself sets the
605	    expectation the opened descriptor is then proved against.  A symlink
606	    swapped in at any point fails the export identifying ``display`` as
607	    a directory that changed into a symlink, and its target — outside
608	    the tree, inside it, or the moved original — is never touched.
609	    """
610	    return _open_confirmed_directory(
611	        parent_fd, name, display, expected=None, during_scan=True
612	    )

614	
615	def _open_confirmed_directory(
616	    parent_fd: int,
617	    name: str,
618	    display: Path,
619	    expected: tuple[int, int] | None,
620	    during_scan: bool,
621	) -> int:
622	    """Open ``name`` relative to ``parent_fd`` and pin the directory.
623	
624	    The single confirmation rule shared by the lookup and the package
625	    copy: the name is inspected with ``fstatat`` without following
626	    symlinks and then opened with ``openat`` using ``O_NOFOLLOW`` and
627	    ``O_DIRECTORY``; the descriptor is fstat()ed and proved to be the
628	    directory the inspection named.  ``expected`` carries the
629	    ``(device, inode)`` the binding must match — the identity recorded
630	    during the lookup when the copy re-checks an already confirmed
631	    directory, or ``None`` when the lookup confirms a directory for the
632	    first time and the fresh inspection itself is the expectation.
633	
634	    ``during_scan`` selects the phase the error messages report:
635	    failures while walking the tree say "during scan" and "cannot scan",
636	    failures while copying the package say "during export" and "cannot
637	    inspect".  A symlink swapped in at any point in this sequence fails
638	    the export identifying ``display`` and what it became; the link's
639	    target is never touched.
640	    """
641	    try:
642	        before = os.stat(name, dir_fd=parent_fd, follow_symlinks=False)
643	    except OSError as error:
644	        raise ExportError(f"cannot inspect directory {display}: {error}") from error
645	    if expected is None:
646	        expected = (before.st_dev, before.st_ino)
647	    if (
648	        stat.S_ISLNK(before.st_mode)
649	        or not stat.S_ISDIR(before.st_mode)
650	        or (before.st_dev, before.st_ino) != expected
651	    ):
652	        raise _directory_changed_message(
653	            display, before.st_mode, during_scan=during_scan
654	        )
655	    try:
656	        descriptor = os.open(
657	            name,
658	            os.O_RDONLY | _O_NOFOLLOW | _O_DIRECTORY,
659	            dir_fd=parent_fd,
660	        )
661	    except OSError as error:
662	        if error.errno in (errno.ELOOP, errno.ENOTDIR):
663	            # The path changed between the fstatat and the open; inspect
664	            # it once more to report the concrete reason.
665	            raise _directory_changed_error(
666	                parent_fd, name, display, during_scan=during_scan
667	            ) from error
668	        raise _directory_access_error(display, error, during_scan) from error
669	    try:
670	        opened = os.fstat(descriptor)
671	    except OSError as error:
672	        os.close(descriptor)
673	        raise _directory_access_error(display, error, during_scan) from error
674	    if not stat.S_ISDIR(opened.st_mode) or (
675	        opened.st_dev,
676	        opened.st_ino,
677	    ) != expected:
678	        os.close(descriptor)
679	        raise _directory_changed_error(
680	            parent_fd, name, display, during_scan=during_scan
681	        )
682	    return descriptor
683	
684	
685	def _directory_access_error(
686	    display: Path, error: OSError, during_scan: bool
687	) -> ExportError:
688	    """Report a directory that cannot be entered, naming the phase."""
689	    action = "scan" if during_scan else "inspect"
690	    return ExportError(f"cannot {action} directory {display}: {error}")

697	    try:
698	        now = os.stat(name, dir_fd=parent_fd, follow_symlinks=False)
699	    except OSError as error:

701	    try:

703	    except OSError as error:
704	        raise ExportError(f"cannot scan directory {display}: {error}") from error
705	    if (now.st_dev, now.st_ino) != (pinned.st_dev, pinned.st_ino):

711	def _directory_changed_error(
712	    parent_fd: int, name: str, display: Path, during_scan: bool
713	) -> ExportError:
714	    """Build the change error, inspecting the swapped path once for the reason."""
715	    try:
716	        now = os.stat(name, dir_fd=parent_fd, follow_symlinks=False)

719	        mode = None

723	def _directory_changed_message(
724	    display: Path, mode: int | None, during_scan: bool
725	) -> ExportError:
726	    """Fail naming the directory that changed and what it became."""
727	    phase = "during scan" if during_scan else "during export"
728	    if mode is not None and stat.S_ISLNK(mode):
729	        reason = "is now a symlink"
730	    elif mode is not None and stat.S_ISDIR(mode):
731	        reason = "was replaced by a different directory"
732	    else:
733	        reason = "no longer points to the directory being scanned"
734	    return ExportError(f"directory changed {phase}: {display} {reason}")

737	class _SourceAnchor:
738	    """Pinned view of the confirmed source tree, used while copying.
739	
740	    Holds the root descriptor for the whole export and the identity of
741	    every directory observed during the lookup.  Each verification
742	    re-derives directory bindings from descriptors (``fstatat`` and
743	    ``openat`` with ``O_NOFOLLOW``/``O_DIRECTORY``) instead of trusting
744	    path strings, so a real directory replaced by a symlink after the
745	    lookup — before a sample is opened, while it is read or between
746	    samples — fails the export even when the link leads to byte-equal
747	    content.  :meth:`verify_all` runs once more after every sample has
748	    been copied, so the package is never published when a binding
749	    changed.
750	    """
751	
752	    def __init__(
753	        self,
754	        root_fd: int,
755	        root: Path,
756	        directories: dict[str, tuple[Path, int, int]],
757	    ) -> None:
758	        self.root_fd = root_fd
759	        self.root = root
760	        self.directories = directories
761	
762	    def verify_file(self, source: Path) -> None:
763	        """Prove the root and all ancestor directories of ``source``."""
764	        parts = source.relative_to(self.root).parts[:-1]
765	        self._descend(tuple(parts))
766	
767	    def verify_all(self) -> None:
768	        """Prove the root and every directory recorded during the lookup.
769	
770	        A single descriptor-anchored traversal over the recorded
771	        parent/child structure opens each directory exactly once, so a
772	        tree of any depth costs one descent rather than one per
773	        directory.  Every open is an ``openat`` relative to the pinned
774	        parent, so a symlink swapped in at any level is refused.  The
775	        descent runs on an explicit stack rather than Python calls, so a
776	        tree deeper than the interpreter's recursion limit is verified
777	        in full instead of aborting partway with a ``RecursionError``.
778	        """
779	        self._check_root()
780	        children: dict[str, list[tuple[str, str]]] = {}
781	        for key in self.directories:
782	            if not key:
783	                continue
784	            parent_key, _, name = key.rpartition("/")
785	            children.setdefault(parent_key, []).append((name, key))
786	        # A frame is one opened directory: its descriptor, whether this
787	        # traversal owns that descriptor (the root's is held by the
788	        # export), the children still to verify (reversed, so pop()
789	        # yields sorted order) and its display path.  Parent frames stay
790	        # on the stack while their subtree is verified, so each
791	        # directory is pinned for exactly as long as a recursive
792	        # traversal would hold it, at any depth.
793	        frames: list[tuple[int, bool, list[tuple[str, str]], Path]] = [

896	    directory_fd: int, name: str, path: Path

902	    then opened with ``openat`` plus ``O_NOFOLLOW`` and ``O_NONBLOCK``;
903	    the descriptor is fstat()ed and proved to be that same object
904	    before any byte is read.  Closing the inspect/open gap this way
905	    means an object swapped in after the walk typed the entry — a
906	    named pipe, even one with no writer or one whose writer would
907	    supply the planned bytes, a symlink, or another regular file, even
908	    one with identical content, size and modification time — fails the
909	    export immediately: the open never waits for a writer, the swapped
910	    object's bytes are never hashed, and the error names this path.
911	    The recorded identity is the proved descriptor's
912	    ``(device, inode)`` — the object the bytes actually came from —
913	    which the copy later independently re-pins before streaming the
914	    package.  Any failure raises with the path and reason.  Returns
915	    ``(digest, device, inode)``.

918	    :mod:`confirmed`, shared with import; only the export wording is
919	    assembled here.

922	        confirmed_status = confirmed.inspect_regular(name, dir_fd=directory_fd)
923	        descriptor = confirmed.open_without_follow(name, dir_fd=directory_fd)

925	        # success it also clears the open's temporary O_NONBLOCK, so the
926	        # descriptor hash_descriptor streams is an ordinary blocking one.
927	        opened = confirmed.prove_opened_regular(descriptor, confirmed_status)

932	            ) from failure

1039	def _assert_target_name_free(target: Path) -> None:

1057	def _publish_package(temp_path: Path, target: Path) -> None:
1058	    """Publish the finished package without ever replacing the target name.
1059	
1060	    The package is complete and source-verified by the time this runs.
1061	    The name is re-checked and then claimed with a single ``link(2)``,
1062	    which creates a new directory entry and fails with ``EEXIST`` when the
1063	    name is occupied by anything at all — a regular file, a directory or
1064	    a symlink, including one whose target does not exist.  A file another
1065	    program creates at the last instant — even an empty one or one
1066	    byte-identical to the package — is therefore never replaced, unlinked
1067	    or written through.  The package lives in the same directory as the
1068	    target, so the link is same-filesystem and a reader can only ever see
1069	    the complete file; this run's temporary link is removed afterwards,
1070	    leaving the occupant untouched on conflict.
1071	    """
1072	    _assert_target_name_free(target)
1073	    try:
1074	        os.link(temp_path, target)
1075	    except FileExistsError:
1076	        # The name was claimed in the gap after the check: link refused
1077	        # it atomically, so the occupant — file or symlink of any kind —
1078	        # is exactly as the other program left it.
1079	        raise ExportError(f"target already exists: {target}") from None
1080	    except OSError as error:
1081	        raise ExportError(f"cannot write export package: {error}") from error
1082	    # The target now carries the finished package under its own link.
1083	    # Drop the temporary link; if even that fails the package is already
1084	    # published, so the export still succeeds.
1085	    try:
1086	        os.unlink(temp_path)
1087	    except OSError:
1088	        pass

1091	def _write_package(

1093	    classes: dict[str, str],
1094	    members: list[dict[str, Any]],
1095	    manifest: dict[str, Any],
1096	    resolver: dict[str, tuple[Path, int, int]] | None = None,
1097	    source_anchor: _SourceAnchor | None = None,
1098	) -> None:

1101	    The target is never overwritten: an occupied target is rejected both
1102	    when the export starts and once the package is finished, and the
1103	    finished package is claimed with a non-replacing ``link`` rather than
1104	    a rename, so a file or symlink (even a dangling one) that another
1105	    program creates while the images are copied is preserved and the
1106	    export fails naming the target.  Streaming to a temp file until the
1107	    whole package has been written, fsynced and source-verified means a
1108	    failure or interruption leaves neither an incomplete target nor this
1109	    run's temp file.  An flock on a lock file next to the target
1110	    serializes concurrent exports to the same path.
1111	    """
1112	    target = Path(target)
1113	    parent = target.parent
1114	    try:
1115	        parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
1116	    except OSError as error:
1117	        raise ExportError(f"cannot create target directory {parent}: {error}") from error
1118	
1119	    lock_path = target.with_name(f".{target.name}.lock")
1120	    try:
1121	        lock_descriptor = os.open(lock_path, os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT, 0o600)
1122	    except OSError as error:
1123	        raise ExportError(f"cannot lock target {target}: {error}") from error
1124	
1125	    temp_path: Path | None = None
1126	    try:
1127	        fcntl.flock(lock_descriptor, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
1128	        _assert_target_name_free(target)
1129	
1130	        fd, temp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(
1131	            prefix=f".{target.name}.", suffix=".tmp", dir=parent
1132	        )
1133	        temp_path = Path(temp_name)

1135	            with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as stream:
1136	                _write_zip(
1137	                    stream,
1138	                    classes,
1139	                    members,
1140	                    manifest,
1141	                    resolver,
1142	                    source_anchor=source_anchor,

1151	                # temp file is discarded rather than published.

1167	            fcntl.flock(lock_descriptor, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
1168	        finally:
